headline: Isomorphic Labs, the AI drug-design company spun out of Google DeepMind, is reportedly in early talks to raise money at a valuation of $40 billion to $50 billion.
score_reason: Large reported valuation for AI drug discovery, but early talks reported by one outlet and no deal; kept at the curator score.
importance_line: Shows how much investors will bet on AI-designed medicines, which concerns future patients and drug developers, but Isomorphic has yet to test its own drug candidates in humans and the talks may not close.
summary: Bloomberg reports, as relayed by City AM, that Isomorphic Labs, a London company that uses AI to design medicines, is in early talks to raise new money at a valuation of at least $40 billion that could reach $50 billion, against roughly $17.5 billion before, and no agreement has been reached. The company has not yet tested its own drug candidates in humans and is aiming for its first clinical trials by the end of 2026.
notes: Read City AM, which credits Bloomberg for the talks; Bloomberg original not opened.
